title: coap_oscore_unprotect_resource_request returns 0 after sending 4.01 on ctx miss; callers double-respond
description: Found while verifying bd 6mij.2.2. coap_oscore.c:62-65: when oscore_ctx_get_by_eui64 fails, the helper sends 4.01 via coap_oscore_send_unauthorized() and returns ITS result, which is 0 (OSCORE_OK) on send success. Documented contract ('return 0 on success, CoAP response code on error') makes callers treat 0 as 'continue'. Example: coap_msg.c msg_sent_post (line ~957) proceeds past ret!=0, then oscore.payload==NULL (memset by helper) triggers coap_oscore_respond_resource(...BAD_REQUEST...) which sends a SECOND response on the wire - the client gets 4.01 then an unprotected 4.00 for one request. Suggested fixes (owner's call): return a nonzero CoAP code after sending so callers return immediately, or have the helper take over response duty exclusively and document that callers must return without responding when result->ctx==NULL and is_protected; audit existing call sites in coap_msg.c either way. Note: /keys handlers (coap_keys.c) avoid this defect by keeping the ctx-miss path inline; if they migrate to the shared helper this must be fixed first.
